failure_family: Layer-B native-owner bootstrap compile ownership and provenance
selected_strategy: Compile one reviewed translation unit to an ELF relocatable object with -c and -save-temps=obj; retain preprocessed, assembly, dependency and object outputs. Link and owner execution remain separate future packets.
why_changed: No collect2, linker, startup object, target libc/pthread library or linker-map provenance is present in this scope.
The preprocessor, compiler and assembler intermediates are persistent named outputs rather than vanished driver temporaries.
The unit still has identity-safe systemd ownership, a sanitized environment, per-process limits, an observation deadline and an independent cleanup budget.
required_supervision: Capture active/exited success and stable InvocationID before immediate stop.
Use a separate 30-second cleanup budget after the compile observation deadline.
A stop timeout, error or ambiguous state triggers a separate manager-side SIGKILL of the unit control group.
Accept either loaded/inactive or unloaded/not-found only after successful stop and empty or absent original cgroup membership.
Uncertain submission, inaccessible ownership evidence or residual membership is FAIL_UNRESOLVED and is never retried.
provenance_scope: Bind source, source-model test, selected controller/compiler tools, three explicit system-header roots, actual .d prerequisites and the cc1/assembler chain from -v. Generated .i/.s/.o/.d files are outputs; private disappearing scratch entries are recorded as ephemeral, not fabricated persistent inputs.
limitations: This is not a hermetic full compiler runtime-library/file-open trace.
It does not establish link success, owner execution, network isolation, aggregate resource limits or OS acceptance.
